html:
The Zaporozhian Sich was the fortified camp and self ruling host of the Zaporozhian Cossacks, on islands below the rapids of the Dnieper in southern Ukraine, from the mid 1500s until Russia destroyed it in 1775.

Its people were mostly runaway peasants and adventurers who lived free of lords on the steppe frontier. They elected their leaders, the hetman and otaman, in open assemblies. They raided Ottoman and Crimean Tatar lands by land and in light boats across the Black Sea, and served Poland or Russia for pay. Their rising under Khmelnytsky created a Cossack state. Catherine the Great had the Sich destroyed in 1775 and moved many Cossacks to the Kuban. Its memory of freedom shaped Ukrainian national identity and inspired Repin's painting of the Cossacks writing an insulting letter to the sultan.
